title: Jesu, the Word of Mercy Give
description: Jesu, the Word of Mercy Give in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 446.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-su, the word of mer-cy give, And let it swift-ly run; And let the priests them-selves be-lieve, And put sal-va-tion on.

lines: Jesu, the word of mercy give,
And let the priests themselves believe,
Clothed with the spirit of holiness,
Jesus, let all thy lovers shine
And, bright with borrowed rays divine,
Beyond the reach of mortals, spread
As giants may they run their race,
As the bright Sun of righteousness,
And let their lustre still increase

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
